function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I don’t have direct access to a reverse‑geocoding service from within this environment, so I can’t pull the address for you in real time.  
However, you can easily get that information yourself using a public geocoding API. Below are a couple of common options and a quick example of how to call them.

---

## 1. Google Maps Geocoding API

**Endpoint**

```
https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

**What you’ll get**

A JSON response that includes the formatted address, plus detailed address components (street, city, state, country, etc.).

**Example (curl)**

```bash
curl "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY"
```

**Result snippet**

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

> **Note:** You’ll need to replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with a valid Google Maps API key. The free tier allows a limited number of requests per day.

---

## 2. OpenStreetMap Nominatim (free, no key required)

**Endpoint**

```
https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499
```

**Example (curl)**

```bash
curl "https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499"
```

**Result snippet**

```json
{
  "place_id": "123456789",
  "licence": "Data © OpenStreetMap contributors",
  "osm_type": "way",
  "osm_id": "987654321",
  "lat": "37.4224764",
  "lon": "-122.0842499",
  "display_name": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States",
  "address": {
    "house_number": "1600",
    "road": "Amphitheatre Parkway",
    "city": "Mountain View",
    "county": "Santa Clara County",
    "state": "California",
    "postcode": "94043",
    "country": "United States",
    "country_code": "us"
  },
  ...
}
```

> **Tip:** Nominatim has usage policies (e.g., no heavy traffic, identify your application). For production use, consider hosting your own instance or using a commercial provider.

---

## Quick Summary

| Service | URL | Key Needed | Typical Response |
|---------|-----|------------|------------------|
| Google Maps Geocoding | `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=...&key=...` | Yes | `formatted_address`, address components |
| OpenStreetMap Nominatim | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=...&lon=...` | No | `display_name`, address components |

Pick the one that best fits your needs (Google for higher accuracy and official data, OSM for free and open data). Once you hit the endpoint, you’ll see the full address for the coordinates you provided.
